questions.stem: Fornix contains which types of fibres?
questions.solutionHtml:
Association, Commissural and Projection

Hippocampal commissure of fornix. The two crura are interconnected by fibres passing from one to another. These crossing fibres interconnect the two hippocampi and form the commissure of fornix/hippocampa! commissure.

  • Some fibres of fornix pass above the splenium of corpus callosum to end in the cingulate gyrus of the same side and constitute the dorsal fornix made up of association fibres.
  • Most of the fibres of fornix are made up of projection fibres connecting the hippocampus with the mamillary body.
  • Thus, fornix consists of three types of white fibres: (a) projection fibres, (b) commissural fibres, and association fibres.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 4, Page No. 176.

questions.stem: Ito cells are present in which part of the liver:
questions.solutionHtml:
Space of Disse
  • The Disse space lies between hepatocytes and the sinusoids and is also referred to as the perisinusoidal space. The Disse space cannot be visualized on an H&E slide from a normal liver but is visible as a narrow tissue space in electron micrographs.
  • Resident cells of the liver include hepatocytes, hepatic stellate cells (also known as fat-storing Ito cells), sinusoidal endothelial cells, macrophages (Kupffer cells), the epithelial cells of the biliary tree (cholangiocytes), hepatic stem cells, natural killer lymphocytes (pit cells), and connective tissue cells of the capsule and portal tracts.

Hepatic stellate cells:

  • Hepatic stellate cells are much less numerous than hepatocytes. They are irregular in outline and lie within the perisinusoidal space of Disse between the sinusoids and the hepatocyte plates. They are thought to be mesenchymal in origin and are characterized by numerous cytoplasmic lipid droplets. These cells secrete most of the intralobular matrix components, including collagen type III (reticular) fibres.

Space of Disse




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1215.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not content of carotid sheath:
questions.solutionHtml:
Sympathetic chain
  • Carotid sheath: Carotid sheath It is a tubular condensation of deep cervical fascia around the (a) common carotid and internal carotid arteries, and (b) internal jugular vein and vagus nerve.
  • The glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) descends from the anterior part of the jugular foramen, running within the carotid sheath at the lateral aspect of the carotid artery.
  • The cervical sympathetic chain is closely related to posterior wall of the sheath, plastered to the prevertebral fascia


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No- 1464.e56.

questions.stem: Superior cerebellar peduncle is at which of the following levels?
questions.solutionHtml:
Midbrain

The superior cerebellar peduncles connect the cerebellum to the midbrain, the middle cerebellar peduncles to the pons, and the inferior cerebellar peduncles to the medulla oblongata.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-456.

Fasciculus Gracilis and Cuneatus
  • The fibres of fasciculus gracilis and fasciculus Cuneatus terminate in nucleus gracilis and nucleus Cuneatus, respectively.
  • The axons of second-order sensory neurons from nucleus gracilis and nucleus Cuneatus curve ventromedially around the central grey matter of the medulla as internal arcuate fibres to undergo decussation.
  • The fibres after crossing the midline turn upwards as a flat tract called medial lemniscus, which courses upwards to terminate in the ventral posterolateral nucleus (VPL) of the thalamus.
  • The third-order sensory neurons from thalamus project into the cerebral cortex of the cerebral hemisphere. This pathway carrying conscious proprioceptive sensations is termed ‘dorsal column—medial lemniscus pathway’.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1464.e17.

questions.stem: Cells Lining the isthmus of gastric pits:
questions.solutionHtml:
Stem cells
  • Stem cells are relatively undifferentiated mitotic cells from which the other types of gland cells are derived. They are relatively few in number, and are situated in the isthmus of the gland and the bases of the gastric pits.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1169, 1170.

questions.solutionHtml:
Sternocleidomastoid

Pretracheal Layer

The pretracheal layer of fascia is situated in the anterior neck. The trachea, oesophagus & thyroid gland are enclosed by the pretracheal fascia.

questions.stem: Transitional epithelium present in all except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Membranous urethra

Urothelium (urinary or transitional epithelium)

  • Urothelium is a specialized epithelium that lines much of the urinary tract and prevents its rather toxic contents from damaging surrounding structures. It extends from the ends of the collecting ducts of the kidneys, through the ureters and bladder, to the proximal portion of the urethra. In males it lines the urethra as far as the ejaculatory ducts, then becomes intermittent and is finally replaced by stratified columnar epithelium in the membranous urethra.

Transitional epithelium




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No- 1281, 1281.e1.

questions.stemHtml: Artery present in close proximity to the marked area?
questions.solutionHtml:
Middle meningeal artery
  • The marked area is the Pterion.
  • Fracture of pterion: The pterion overlies the anterior division of middle meningeal artery, which rupture following a blow in this region to form an extradural hematoma [a clot formation between the skull bone and the dura mater. The clot, if big, may compress the brain leading to unconsciousness or even death. Therefore, it should be removed as early as possible by trephination or craniotomy.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-553.

questions.stem: Difference between exocrine pancreas and parotid:

options.label: B
options.text: Presence of acidophilic serous acini at the tip

options.label: C
options.text: Serous acini supported by basal lamina

questions.solutionHtml:
Absence of striated duct
  • The parotid gland has striated and intercalated intralobular ducts, whereas the pancreas has ONLY the intercalated type
  • The excretory ducts of the parotid gland are STRATIFIED columnar, whereas the excretory duct of the pancreas is SIMPLE columnar
  • The pancreas has ISLETS of LANGERHANS, whereas the parotid does not.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-659.

questions.stem: Injury to which part of internal capsule causes Contralateral hemiplegia:
questions.solutionHtml:
Posterior limb

Posterior limb has the motor fibres for the Upper limb, Lower limb and trunk through the corticospinal tract which crosses at the medulla.
Hence, an infarct of the artery supplying the posterior limb will cause contralateral hemiplegia.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No- 537,538.

questions.stemHtml: On inspiration at which level does the base of the lung touches over the liver as shown in the Image:
questions.solutionHtml:
B

On deep inspiration the Lung bases reach up to the 8th rib which corresponds to the marked area B on the liver.

  • In the Midclavicular line, on deep inspiration, the lungs can expand till the 8th rib as shown in this Image.

Location of Liver and the gallbladder.

  • During deep inspiration the lower border of the lung reaches level B anteriorly.
  • The lower border of the lung extends till the 6th rib in the midclavicular line, 8th rib in mid axillary line and 10th rib in mid scapular line.
  • During quiet breathing, the diaphragm moves about 1.5 cm.
  • During deep breathing; however, it moves by 6-10 cm thus extending up to the level of the 6th rib or 11th thoracic vertebra on the right side.
  • On full expiration, it extends up to 4th costal cartilage anteriorly, posteriorly up to the 8th vertebra.
  • This corresponds to a line dividing the liver in upper 1/3rd and middle 1/3rd marked as B in the given Image.




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-995,996, 996.e1.
